hero.title: Heritage & Mission
hero.description: XINRM: A Legacy of Empowerment and Sustainable Change.

background.title: Heritage & Mission
background.quote: XINRM is a natural extension of the Social Centre's 50-year legacy of empowering people to create change.

vision_fr_bacher.title: The Vision of Fr. Bacher
text: Founded on the vision of the पुणे Jesuits, the Social Centre has spent decades working on knowledge dissemination, community participation, and strategic partnerships.
XINRM builds on this foundation to nurture future leaders in sustainability, bridging the gap between academia and grassroots action.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.text: To address the gaps in the current educational landscape by combining Action Research with academic rigor, directly contributing to India's SDG targets and fostering sustainable rural development.

items.title: Father Herman Bacher established the Social...
items.text: Father Herman Bacher established the Social Centre (SC)with the objective of alleviating the poverty and hardships of the poor farmers through development of water resources and increased agricultural productivity.

items.title: Individual Farmer Phase...
items.text: Individual Farmer Phase

items.title: Social Centre functions as the bridge...
items.text: Social Centre functions as the bridge between the deprived small farmers and local institutions like government, banks, sugar factories, etc.

items.title: Set up an Industrial Training Institute...
items.text: Set up an Industrial Training Institute (ITI) named Electro Technical Institute/Xavier Technical Training Institute (XTTI), in Shrirampur Block of Ahmednagar, which was the first of its kind in the district, to train rural youth in wireman and electrician courses for self-employment.

items.title: Set up the Groundwater Investigation Team...
items.text: Set up the Groundwater Investigation Team (GIT) at Ahmednagar along with 8 other voluntary organisations. The GIT was later taken over by Action for Food Production (AFPRO).

items.title: Constructed of 20 individual wells through...
items.text: Constructed of 20 individual wells through Project Holders (Parishes) under Swiss Caritas.

items.title: In order to blast and dig...
items.text: In order to blast and dig the hard rocks, with a view to complete the incomplete individual wells under Food for Work (FFW) Program, a separate drilling and blasting unit, the Xavier Drilling Team (XDT) was set up in Shrirampur. From the money it generated, XDT supported several development activities of Social Centre including XTTI for more than 18 years.

items.title: Agreement with AFPRO, Ahmednagar Unit to provide hydro
items.text: Agreement with AFPRO, Ahmednagar Unit to provide hydro-geologists for siting wells for irrigation in collaboration with the Ahmednagar District Cooperative Land Development Bank (LDB).

items.title: SC in collaboration with the Pravara...
items.text: SC in collaboration with the Pravara Cooperative Sugar Factory constructed 15 percolation tanks (water harvesting structures) in Pravaranagar area of Ahmednagar in order to trap and store the rainwater. As that time, the construction of percolation tanks was not initiated by the state government in Maharashtra anywhere else. This concept was developed by the government during the drought 1971 and '72. These percolation tanks were constructed through the support of Catholic Relief Services (CRS) under the Food For Work program.

items.title: First Lift Irrigation Systems (LIS)
items.text: First Lift Irrigation Systems (LIS): The Pravara Sugar factory and SC constructed two lift irrigation schemes to lift the surplus canal water during the monsoon season and store it in the newly constructed percolation tanks. This joint venture proved very innovative and successful. These two lift schemes were constructed under the financial support of CRS/USAID.

items.title: Digging of new wells /deepening of old wells
items.text: Digging of new wells /deepening of old wells: Around 700 wells were completed in the district through Project Holders under the CRS Food For Work program.

items.title: Loans to individual farmers
items.text: Loans to individual farmers: Social Centre entered into an agreement with the Ahmednagar District Cooperative Land Development Bank (LDB) for advancing loans to small farmers who were considered unworthy of receiving loans due to insufficient security to mortgage their lands. In addition, interest subsidy was also given to the farmers if they repaid the loan instalment before the due date. To ease the burden on poor farmers, the repayment instalments were designed in such a manner that the farmer's share (capital) was low in the initial years, which increased gradually, and Social Centre's share (interest subsidy) higher, which tapered off gradually.

items.title: Very severe drought in Maharashtra and in some other states.
items.text: Very severe drought in Maharashtra and in some other states. Both open wells, as well as bore wells ran dry. There was famine and large-scale migration and massive cattle deaths.

items.title: 200 community wells were dug under Govt.
items.text: 200 community wells were dug under Govt. of Maharashtra schemes as relief work to provide employment to villagers during the drought period, some of which were left incomplete after the onset of the monsoons in 1974. All the relief work was stopped by the government as the drought had ended.

items.title: Community Cooperation Phase
items.text: Community Cooperation Phase:

items.title: Community Lift Irrigation Schemes
items.text: Community Lift Irrigation Schemes: SC, in collaboration with the ADCC Bank, the Revenue Department, the Zilla Parishad (ZP) (district council)/Panchayat Samiti (block-level governing body) and the people themselves, undertook the deepening and completion of 30 incomplete community wells which were initiated under the government scheme during the drought period. The  community lift irrigation schemes were completed by securing bank loans for installing electric pumps and laying pipelines, as well as for providing crop loans. The beneficiaries were brought together into cooperative users' societies.

items.title: Ahmednagar District Central Co
items.text: Ahmednagar District Central Co-operative (ADCC) Bank Loans for Community lift irrigation schemes: After successful completion of the 30 community lift irrigation schemes, the program was expanded on a large scale. SC entered into an agreement with the ADCC Bank for providing loans to farmers for community lift irrigation schemes. In order to avail of credit facilities, a farmer had now to become a member of the local cooperative Village Multipurpose Services Cooperative Society (MSCS), also known as Primary Agricultural Credit Society or PACS. It was only through these societies that loans were disbursed.

items.title: Lift Irrigation Phase
items.text: Lift Irrigation Phase: Once the success of these community LIS became apparent, SC and ADCC Bank began financing the larger community LIS in the district. Small farmers along the Pravara and Mula Rivers were organised into cooperative lift irrigation societies to undertake 150 group lift irrigation schemes. More than 100 cooperative lift irrigation societies were formed with one apex body or federation of these societies, paving the way for the linkages of farmers with government agencies, with technical support from cooperative sugar factories in the area. Besides this, 7 large community LISs were completed through loans from ADCC Bank in collaboration with Pravaranagar Sugar Factory with 50% Central Government subsidy for the small farmers under the Drought Prone Area Development Program (DPAP).

items.title: Ahmednagar District experienced another severe drought...
items.text: Ahmednagar District experienced another severe drought and irrigation water was severely restricted. This dealt a blow to the lift irrigation projects. This experience led the SC to rethink its policy on irrigation and look for alternatives that would ensure better drought proofing for the community and environment.

items.title: Preventive Health Care Program
items.text: Preventive Health Care Program: This was initiated in the year 1982, with a view to improving the health care of the rural people with an emphasis on health education. Dispensaries/hospitals run by religious sisters were established in different parts of Ahmednagar district. SC collaborated with Comprehensive Rural Health Project (CRHP) Jamkhed in Ahmednagar District to train the religious sisters along with Community Health Guides in preventive health care. The religious sisters thus trained ran 11 centres in the district which became Community Health Guide Training Centres. Through these centres, SC provided handholding support to 326 Community Health Guides and monitored their work covering 203 villages. Some women's Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and tailoring classes for women were also started at this time.

items.title: Cluster Village Phase
items.text: Cluster Village Phase - Shifting from resource-endowed to poorer, drought-stricken areas

items.title: The Government of Maharashtra launched a...
items.text: The Government of Maharashtra launched a revolutionary program, the Comprehensive Watershed Development Program (COWDEP) in 1982 by passing a resolution which outlined comprehensive land and water management as the key to drought proofing. SC published a booklet to create awareness among villagers about COWDEP.

items.title: Evaluation by Jesuit Evaluation Team.
items.text: Evaluation by Jesuit Evaluation Team.

items.title: An evaluation was commissioned by Swiss...
items.text: An evaluation was commissioned by Swiss Development Cooperation (SDC) through the Indian Institute of Management (IIM), Ahmedabad. This evaluation was participatory, involving the SC staff to critically evaluate whether the objectives of SC had been achieved. A workshop was held to discuss the findings of the IIM evaluation, review SC's past activities and brainstorm about the new policy of SC going forward.

items.title: These evaluations recommended that SC move...
items.text: These evaluations recommended that SC move into the dry areas of Ahmednagar, adopting the cluster village approach, focusing on remote/unreached villages, striving to bring about discriminative justice and taking on the role of facilitator rather than donor.

items.title: May 1984
items.text: Six areas were selected for the participatory village development works based on the cluster approach in Ahmednagar District in Nagar, Parner, Shrigonda, Akole and Sangamner blocks.

items.title: Began building rapport with farmers in...
items.text: Began building rapport with farmers in the new areas through dialogue and problem analysis and engaging them in dryland farming techniques.

items.title: Visit by SC staff to Adgaon...
items.text: Visit by SC staff to Adgaon Watershed project implemented by Marathwada Sheti Sahayya Mandal (MSSM) with technical support from AFPRO involving treatment on wastelands and farmlands, a series of check dams on the drainage line and dryland farming. The impact of the work was clearly visible, and this helped SC realise the need for similar work in its own project villages.

items.title: SC was involved in the Central...
items.text: SC was involved in the Central Government's Integrated Rural Development Program-Below Poverty Line (IRDP-BPL) survey sponsored by SDC and conducted by the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD). The study recommended providing credit without the need for collateral to non-creditworthy BPL households, and further led to subsidised loans by the Central Government to BPL households for income generation.

items.title: Genesis of new ideas, innovations and concepts
items.text: Genesis of new ideas, innovations and concepts: Role model for Watershed Development Projects

items.title: Sep. 1987
items.text: Rural Women's Workshop at Palaspur. Reality maps were drawn using rangoli (traditional sand art) -a precursor to Participatory Rural Appraisal (PRA) maps - to list developmental activities to counter drought from women's perspective. Mr. Anilkumar Gupta from IIM Ahmedabad attended the workshop.

items.title: Dec. 1987
items.text: State-level Workshop of Voluntary Organisations on Drought Action by Social Centre at the Centre for Studies in Rural Development (CSRD), Ahmednagar established Social Centre as an important entity on the map of policy and program dialogue in Maharashtra. The workshop aimed at introducing the concept of watershed development and sharing pragmatic options with the participants. This paved the way for Social Centre's coordination role between voluntary organisations, government officials and policy makers in the Indo-Delhi Watershed Development Programme (IGWDP) two years later.DelhiDelhi

items.title: Dryland farming and crop insurance
items.text: Dryland farming and crop insurance: Social Centre developed various dryland farming practices with technical inputs from Mahatma Phule Krushi Vidyapeeth (Agriculture University) (MPKV) which were promoted among the dryland farmers in the six cluster areas. Scientists from MPKV also helped in guiding the farmers in the use of these techniques. The hesitation of the farmers was overcome by providing crop insurance linked to the technology adoption. It was an innovative, first of its kind scheme developed by Social Centre to cover the risk associated with a new technology. It went a long way in encouraging the adoption of these new technologies.

items.title: Technical leadership
items.text: Technical leadership: SC staff underwent training from AFPRO Geohydrological Investigation Team (GIT) in the practical aspects of watershed development. These first-generation technologists went on to become pioneers in watershed development planning in Maharashtra, particularly to build the capacities of voluntary organisations in the IGWDP. The concept was later adopted by WOTR in the form of Panlot Sevaks (Watershed Volunteers) in the IGWDP.

items.title: September 1988
items.text: On September 9, 1988, the second state-level workshop on drought was held at Water and Land Management Institute (WALMI), Aurangabad in which 50 voluntary organisations and five funding agencies participated. The aim of this workshop was to discuss, in the light of the drought of 1987, how NGOs could respond to mitigate the impact of future drought. It was designed to showcase best practices like Social Centre's dryland farming pilot, the Adgaon watershed of MSSM, and soil and water conservation practices in the Konkan region by Gram Gaurav Pratishthan, with a view towards long-term drought proofing. The workshop was organised by MSSM and supported by Action for Agricultural Renewal in Maharashtra (AFARM) and AFPRO. Father Bacher was present as the representative from MISERIOR, New Delhi.

items.title: First watershed development venture.
items.text: First watershed development venture. Kasare was the first village where the scientific approach of participatory watershed works was initiated, followed by Pimpalgaon Wagha and then Mendhvan. These villages were the field laboratory for incubation of new ideas, community participation and record-keeping systems and later became role models for replication and implementation of the IGWDP in Maharashtra.

items.title: Government soil and water conservation schemes...
items.text: Government soil and water conservation schemes were implemented in these villages through SC.

items.title: Community
items.text: Community-Based Organisations (CBOs) and systems in Kasare: Setting up of women's groups, farmers' groups, youth groups in the villages. Kasare was the training ground where such institutions emerged and thrived. A Thrift and Credit Group was set up of 105 women. Social Centre, along with Chaitanya, Rajgurunagar, developed record-keeping systems for these groups. These systems, perhaps a first example of co-creation of accounting tools for grassroots groups, formed the basis of future record-keeping systems adopted by the SHG movement in various parts of India. Different activities such as raising nurseries, plantation and income generation activities were promoted through the women's groups.

items.title: Youth and farmers also took up the self
items.text: Youth and farmers also took up the self-financed initiative of growing fodder collectively to meet the needs of the village. This was an early example of group farming.

items.title: The Gramseva Tarun Mandal (village youth group) also established a self
items.text: The Gramseva Tarun Mandal (village youth group) also established a self-financed nursery to provide saplings for afforestation work in the village. This activity of setting up a nursery in the village became an essential strategy in future watershed programmes.

items.title: The Kasare Mahila Mandal (women's group)...
items.text: The Kasare Mahila Mandal (women's group) was highly motivated and came forward for watershed development work. This was a first for women in the state. All the women actively participated in the watershed work in the village through shramadan (voluntary labour) for excavating contour trenches. They also developed a plot in the village through shramadan, undertaking tree plantation on it. This marked the beginning of active women's participation in natural resource management activities in all of Maharashtra.

items.title: This Kasare pattern of engaging local...
items.text: This Kasare pattern of engaging local CBOs in the mainstream development of the village became a standard practice in later watershed development projects. Thus, Social Centre was able to demonstrate an approach of strengthening local CBOs to take charge of the development of their village by taking the participatory planning and implementation to the next level.

items.title: Collaboration and Joint Action
items.text: Collaboration and Joint Action: Under SC's coordination, four voluntary organisations, CSRD, Bosco Gramin Vikas Kendra (BGVK), Tata Relief Committee (TRC) and Social Centre came together to work in 4 villages (Pimpri Gauli, Dongargan, Dhotre Khurd and Kakanewadi) as one project. The initial funding of Rs. 20 lakhs was provided by the Indo-German Social Service Society (IGSSS) and the remaining larger funding was provided by EZE (Evangelische Zentralstelle für Entwicklungshilfe eV or the Protestant Association for Cooperation in Development), Germany. It was the first collaborative project in watershed development, and probably formed the basis for the future two-phase approach in the IGWDP (Capacity Building Phase and Full Implementation Phase).

items.title: Comprehensive Area
items.text: Comprehensive Area-based Program Phase- Watershed Development - from resource exploitation to resource mobilisation

items.title: As awareness increased regarding the intimate...
items.text: As awareness increased regarding the intimate link between the degradation of natural resource and poverty, SC decided to change its approach from resource exploitation to resource mobilisation (conservation and management), from sectorial interventions to comprehensive, integrated area-based resource development. The natural unit for such interventions is the micro-watershed, which forms the subsistence space of the village and which is their area of survival.

items.title: Village Community Action for Comprehensive Micro
items.text: Village Community Action for Comprehensive Micro-Watershed Development through IGSSS and Government of Germany in Maharashtra. In the initial stage, 6 villages were selected under the cluster approach, and the community's capacities were built to undertake watershed works in their village. Financial support was provided by the IGSSS, New Delhi.

items.title: Exposure Dialogue Programs provided space for...
items.text: Exposure Dialogue Programs provided space for international policy makers to live with the rural community and have close interaction with individuals and people's institutions like the Village Watershed Committee (VWC), SHGs, youth groups etc. The relevance of watershed development as a strategy to alleviate poverty became evident after this exposure, and this created opportunities to influence watershed development, as well as participatory natural resources management efforts on the international front.

items.title: Incubating IGWDP
items.text: Incubating IGWDP - After seeing the huge impact of the watershed work undertaken so far in drought-stricken villages in Ahmednagar, Father Bacher was fully convinced that watershed development based on the Ridge-to-Valley concept is the only solution to mitigating the effects of drought. Social Centre and Father Bacher came to the conclusion that drought proofing in the long run could only be achieved through natural resource regeneration along watershed lines involving the people's participation at all levels of project implementation.

items.title: Father Bacher's initiative to promote Participatory...
items.text: Father Bacher's initiative to promote Participatory Watershed Development Program: The Indo-German Watershed Programme was visualised and initiated by Fr. Bacher. It was funded under a bilateral agreement between the Government of Germany and Government of India and implemented by the KfW (Kreditanstalt für Wiederaufbau or German Development Bank) and NABARD. In the initial years, the coordination of the Capacity Building Phase of the IGWDP was done by SC, which later shifted to the Watershed Organisation Trust (WOTR), after its establishment in 1993 specifically for this purpose.

items.title: Under the IGWDP, SC successfully completed...
items.text: Under the IGWDP, SC successfully completed 16 watershed projects, 13 projects in 3 blocks of Ahmednagar district and 3 projects in the Ashti block of Beed district.

items.title: 1992 and 1998
items.text: Dr. P. C. Alexander (then Governor of Maharashtra) visited Social Centre's watershed project Mendhwan in 1992 and Sherikoldara in 1998.

items.title: In recognition of his outstanding efforts...
items.text: In recognition of his outstanding efforts and contribution to development and cooperation between Germany and India, Fr. Bacher was awarded the Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany (Correct name to be confirmed) at Mendhwan by Mr. Carl Spranger, Minister for Economic Cooperation and Development, Germany.

items.title: Visit of Mr Carl Spranger and Mr.
items.text: Visit of Mr Carl Spranger and Mr. Harshvardhan Deshmukh, Minister of Water Conservation, Government of Maharashtra to Mendhwan and Kasare.

items.title: After the visit to Mendhavan and...
items.text: After the visit to Mendhavan and Kasare villages, the Minister for Economic Cooperation and Development, Germany, signed the agreement in New Delhi with Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao for the financial support of Rs. 100 crores (1 billion) for the IGWDP and Rs. 300 cores to the Central Government for various development projects.

items.title: Project Sanctioning and Steering Committee (PSSC)...
items.text: Project Sanctioning and Steering Committee (PSSC) set up for the sanctioning of NABARD funds under the Full Implementation Phase of the IGWDP projects. SC was one of the members of the PSSC from the inception of the IGWDP till March 2009 along with WOTR.

items.title: Area Plan for Rural Industrialisation (APRI)
items.text: Area Plan for Rural Industrialisation (APRI): Social Centre was the nodal agency for NABARD for providing support for rural industrialisation through APRI. It was unique in that it combined strengthening the existing credit delivery system and blending it with the provision of non-financial services like motivation and coordination which were provided by SC. The target groups of this project were potential entrepreneurs in rural areas comprising artisans, craftsmen, landless, tribal, and other weaker sections of society, as well as the existing rural industrial units.

items.title: Change in SC strategy and decision...
items.text: Change in SC strategy and decision to implement watershed activities with the convergence and linkages of government funds: Watershed activities were undertaken in 13 villages in this manner with convergence and linkages of government funds with SC providing the shortfall funds.

items.title: Christian Aid sanctioned the Comprehensive Watershed...
items.text: Christian Aid sanctioned the Comprehensive Watershed Development Project in Kaknewadi in 1992, which was completed in 1996.

items.title: The Govt.
items.text: The Govt. of India's Drought Prone Area Program (DPAP) Watershed Program was undertaken in 9 villages.

items.title: Focus on Women's empowerment.
items.text: Focus on Women's empowerment. In order to mainstream women into the development process, SC focused its efforts on developing the capacities of women to enable them to actively participate and take up the responsibility for integrated and sustainable development. Women were formed into SHGs for savings and credit. A Women's Training Centre was set up at Social Centre, Ahmednagar, where women underwent skill and entrepreneurship development trainings. Preventive health trainings and health camps were also conducted, and well as information regarding herbal medicine and acupressure provided.

items.title: SC's role as Regional Resource Centre for IGWDP.
items.text: SC's role as Regional Resource Centre for IGWDP. The responsibilities included identifying reputed NGOs in the region to promote watershed development activities, support the NGO for selection of the watershed villages, build the capacities of the NGO staff, as well as of the village community to carry out the watershed development activities under the Capacity Building Phase of the IGWDP. In this role, besides Ahmednagar, Beed, Satara and Pune districts also came under its purview.

items.title: Expansion of area of operation beyond...
items.text: Expansion of area of operation beyond Ahmednagar district to include neighbouring Beed district. A total of 4 villages were undertaken in the Ashti block of Beed district under the IGWDP. (Can we include some explanation as to why it was decided to expand into Beed?)

items.title: The Food Security and Nutritional Improvement...
items.text: The Food Security and Nutritional Improvement Program was implemented successfully by SC in 3 villages under financial support of Church's Auxiliary for Social Action (CASA).

items.title: Food Security, Women and Child Development project through MISEREOR Germany.
items.text: Food Security, Women and Child Development project through MISEREOR Germany. This project was aimed exclusively at the Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe and nomadic and disadvantaged communities. 11 villages were selected where all the families came under this category, and watershed development and drinking water projects were undertaken.

items.title: Ashankur Rural Women's Training Centre at Bhokar, Shrirampur.
items.text: Ashankur Rural Women's Training Centre at Bhokar, Shrirampur. This was constructed and established by Social Centre with financial support from Christian Aid to provide skill training to rural women. The centre has now been handed over to the Sacred Heart Sisters of Haregaon, who are running it efficiently.

items.title: Water Supply and Sanitation Program under...
items.text: Water Supply and Sanitation Program under Aple Pani Drinking Water Project funded by KfW, Germany through Govt. of Maharashtra. SC was one of the NGOs involved in undertaking a feasibility survey for this project. The project involved construction of water storage tanks, underground pipelines, digging and construction of water source wells, construction of pump houses, stand posts, installation of electric pumps, as well as building the capacity of the village community to effectively manage and maintain the project. SC successfully completed the work in 10 villages, which became model villages for others to learn from and replicate.

items.title: Community
items.text: Community-Focused Child Development Program (CFCDP) funded by Holistic Child Development in India (HCDI) - Phase 1. SC implemented this project in 12 very remote and interior tribal villages/hamlets in Parner and Rahuri blocks of Ahmednagar district. The project aimed at improving the quality of life of the child through improving the lifestyle and opportunities of the family, which in turn was achieved by natural resources management along watershed lines. Seeing the enormous success of the project, HCDI decided to implement watershed development in its other projects throughout India, for which SC deputed one of its experienced engineers to support them.

items.title: Legal Aid Centre
items.text: Legal Aid Centre - (Details to be added)

items.title: Watershed Training Centre at Hivrekorda was...
items.text: Watershed Training Centre at Hivrekorda was established with financial assistance from Manos Unidas. Constructed in a completed watershed, it provides live watershed experience to trainees. SC conducts a broad range of training programs for development of practitioners, from different states, community-based organisations, students and villagers.  SC offers project-based, as well as demand based and sponsored training programs for the participants. Trainings regarding watershed-based natural resource management, community mobilisation, livelihood and entrepreneurship development are also conducted for SC project villages and other NGOs.

items.title: September 14, 2023
items.text: September 14, 2023 - The training centre has been renovated and renamed as Bacher Eco-Training Centre on the occasion of Fr. Bacher's  second death anniversary of

items.title: NABARD Pilot Project for Integrated Development of Backward Blocks (PPID)
items.text: NABARD Pilot Project for Integrated Development of Backward Blocks (PPID) - Phase 1 -The objective of this project was comprehensive development of the selected backward blocks in an integrated manner which included economic development, infrastructure development and other aspects of human development, i.e., education, health, drinking water supply, etc. This necessitated the involvement of all agencies working at grassroot level such as state government agencies, including Gram Panchayats (village governing bodies), banks, NGOs, people's organisations and other development agencies. SC implemented this project in 1 village. Activities under the project included watershed development, NFS (non-farm sector) program, microfinance, farmers' groups under Govt. of India's Vikas Volunteer Vahini (VVV), infrastructure development under Rural Infrastructure Development Program (RIDF), capacity building of banks, government departments, NGOs and community-based organisations, improved coordination with government departments for village developmental activities, such as education, health, women and child development, etc.

items.title: IGWDP - Phase 3.
items.text: IGWDP - Phase 3. A total of 6 watershed villages of Beed district were included in this phase.

items.title: PRA for Bharat Nirmal Drinking Water Program.
items.text: PRA for Bharat Nirmal Drinking Water Program. This was a Central Government program launched by the State Government through the local Gram Panchayats. SC was requested by the Zilla Parishad to conduct PRAs for needs assessment in 12 village in Parner Block of Ahmednagar.

items.title: National Holistic Watershed Development Program (NHWDP)...
items.text: National Holistic Watershed Development Program (NHWDP) in Vidarbha Region (Amravati and Akola Districts). The main objective of the program was to stabilise the livelihood support system of the farming community to reduce the suicides of the farmers through a holistic watershed development program. Besides soil and water conservation activities, the project also aimed at the overall development of families through various supporting activities of livestock development, Wadi development (horticulture plantation), women's welfare activities and improvements in the livelihoods of landless families. SC successfully completed the project in 8 villages.

items.title: Water Supply and Sanitation Program
items.text: Water Supply and Sanitation Program - Phase 2. This phase was implemented by the Government of Maharashtra through the ZP, and included a sanitation and hygiene component. The villages were selected by the ZP, and SC implemented the project in 9 villages. Besides drinking water, the project also included toilets, kitchen gardens and soak pits. As there were no separate funds for these additional activities, SC's major thrust was capacity building the community for these activities. It also helped complete the activities in 50% of the projects through linkages with other ongoing government schemes.

items.title: Food Security, Women and Child Development Project
items.text: Food Security, Women and Child Development Project - Phase 2 through MISEREOR. After successful completion of Phase 1, a second phase was sanctioned by MISEREOR under which work was completed in 9 villages.

items.title: NABARD Pilot Project for Integrated Development of Backward Blocks (PPID)
items.text: NABARD Pilot Project for Integrated Development of Backward Blocks (PPID) - Phase 2. Under this phase, SC implemented the project in 5 villages.

items.title: Community Focused Child Development Program (CFCD) funded by HCDI
items.text: Community Focused Child Development Program (CFCD) funded by HCDI - Phase 2. Under this phase, work was undertaken in 17 new hamlets. 552 children were supported for their basic education, health, nutrition, livelihood and watershed management. Established 12 Early Child Care Centres and handed over to the government through ICDS programme for better stability and continuity. Each village had a children's parliament unit.

items.title: Environment Ecology Enhancement through Drought Proofing...
items.text: Environment Ecology Enhancement through Drought Proofing Activities on Watershed Lines with an Integrated Approach was implemented in 1 village with the financial support of South-Tyrol Autonomous Province of Bolzano, Austria. Under this project mainly land treatment and drainage line treatment activities were carried out with active participation of the village community

items.title: Focus on Climate Change
items.text: Focus on Climate Change:

items.title: SC has been reorienting, re
items.text: SC has been reorienting, re-organising and equipping itself with respect to focus, strategy and interventions in order to specifically address the challenges (and opportunities) posed by climate change to vulnerable rural communities.

items.title: Adivasi Vikas Prakalp
items.text: Adivasi Vikas Prakalp - Gharkul Yojana (Housing Scheme) a total of 55 houses were constructed under the Tribal Development Fund costing of Rs. 100,000 each.

items.title: Under the Second Phase, another 16 houses were constructed by Social Centre.
items.text: Under the Second Phase, another 16 houses were constructed by Social Centre.

items.title: 50 biogas units attached to toilets
items.text: 50 biogas units attached to toilets-cum-bathrooms were constructed in the tribal hamlets of Ahmednagar district (Nagapurwadi, Dubewadi, Palshi, Gawdewadi and Kuttewadi,).

items.title: Integration of Watershed Development Strategies with...
items.text: Integration of Watershed Development Strategies with Climate Change Mitigation for Rehabilitation of Degraded Soils Project completed in 26 tribal villages. The focus was on training people for various sustainable farming methods through demonstration plots, use of alternative energy, judicious use of natural resources, etc.. An Eco Club was established in each village.

items.title: Name of the Project and funder?
items.text: Under the Karanji cluster of Pathardi taluka, ridge-to-valley watershed treatments, organic farming, biogas, multilayer farming, post-watershed management activities , SHGs and livelihood activities were initiated in 7 hamlets having 237 families, covering an area of 450 ha. Twice a month a health check-up camp is conducted with the help of Nityaseva Hospital, Shevgaon in each of these hamlets.

items.title: Similarly, in Satwad cluster consisting of 242 families, an area of 468 ha.
items.text: Similarly, in Satwad cluster consisting of 242 families, an area of 468 ha. was treated. Sustainable farming methods, livelihood activities, alternative energy, kitchen garden, watershed activities along with the promotion of health activities are being implemented.

items.title: Ashakiran Rehabilitation Centre for the HIV/AIDS...
items.text: Ashakiran Rehabilitation Centre for the HIV/AIDS affected orphan children from in and around Ahmednagar district was set up in 2011. The children were given basic education, ITI training, training in various skills like computer, tailoring, nursing, D.Ed, electrician, hospitality management, etc. It has been a home for 32 students for their initial education and training. Most of them are employed today.  It was a successful collaborative venture. It received good support from Jesuit communities, religious, neighbourhood, lay people, parishioners, friends and well-wishers from far and wide. Religious sisters from _______, _______ and _______ helped in running the centre at various times during this period.

items.text: Ashakiran has now been established as a Centre for Alternative Medicine and Medicinal Plants.

items.title: COVID Response
items.text: Special taskforce health activities were implemented during the COVID pandemic period which were found to be very beneficial and effective in saving the lives of the people.

items.title: During the pandemic, 8,942 families were...
items.text: During the pandemic, 8,942 families were supported directly by providing basic necessities for nutrition. Dry fruits, ration materials, sanitation kits, etc. were distributed in the villages in collaboration with the Nuremberg Mission Office, as well as Loyola School, Pune. Health awareness camps were also conducted for them. Besides this, SC collaborated with local government officials, MLAs (local elected representatives), Sarpanchs (village heads) and Gram Panchayat officials to reach out to many needy families in distress. items.title: Established Arrupe Institute of Social Sciences...
items.text: Established Arrupe Institute of Social Sciences Research and Development (AISSRD) at Social Centre to train students from marginalised groups in BSW (Bachelor of Social Work) a graduate degree course under the Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (TMV), Pune. During the period of 2011 to 2016, a total of 93 students have successfully completed this programme. The course was conducted in English/Marathi language. Most of the students were from the Adivasi area. Most of the students got employment in government sector and big companies on higher position. This course found very beneficial to the students.

items.title: The Xavier Institute of Natural Resource...
items.text: The Xavier Institute of Natural Resource Management (XINRM) was established in Ahmednagar to bring to the university academia SC's innovative field practices and lessons learned in the course of working with village communities. The SC team devised the syllabus in 2015 and submitted to the Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU) Academic Council for approval. The course was approved in 2016 and subsequently began at the Ahmednagar Subcentre of the Pune University in 2017. The Social Centre faculty was asked to conduct lectures at the Subcentre. In 2019, Social Centre's XINRM was given special recognition to conduct the course. The institute offers a Master's in Natural Resource Management and Sustainable Development. It also offers different diploma and certificate courses in GIS, Remote Sensing and Natural Resource Management. The NRM course is a blend of classroom teaching and field practicum course. It has a full-fledged soil and water testing lab.

items.title: Action Research Unit
items.text: Action Research Unit: SC is in the process of developing an Action Research Unit to disseminate the field-tested knowledge of six decades to address the pressing needs of society.

items.title: Collaboration with MPKV, Rahuri for Climate Smart Digital Technologies
items.text: Collaboration with MPKV, Rahuri for Climate Smart Digital Technologies: Kasare village has been selected by MPKV, Rahuri for the promotion of Climate Smart Digital Agriculture Village and Climate Smart Digital Technologies developed by MPKV for farmers. A Memorandum of Understanding has been signed between MPKV, Rahuri and Social Centre, Ahmednagar in this regard.
